subject: Delivery profiles & initial rate exception — Nebula POC
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Sara Ortiz <sara.ortiz@nebula.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-10T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Delivery profiles & initial rate exception — Nebula POC

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our discussion, Nebula's POC will have a highly bursty prompt pattern for the first 30–60 seconds of each session (large system prompts + retrieval-heavy context) followed by sustained shorter completions. To keep UX consistent we anticipate needing streaming responses for the demo, but we expect the initial chunk (time-to-first-token) and the sustained tokens/sec to vary from our standard hosted SLA.

Request: would Nebula accept an explicit delivery-profile exception for the POC with the following guardrails?
- TTFT (time-to-first-token): measured p95 per request, target 350ms during peak bursts, with a documented operational variance window.
- Sustained token rate: target 300 tokens/sec per connection p95 for steady-state; allow temporary backpressure to 120 tokens/sec during global capacity spikes.
- Fallback: if streaming cannot meet TTFT target for a given request, Redwood will offer synchronous (batched) delivery for that request and surface a clear flag in the response.
- Pilot period: 30-day evaluation with telemetry export to Nebula for verification.

Attached is a short proposal (redwood-delivery-profiles-proposal-v1.pdf) and a summary of internal microbenchmarks against the workload pattern (nebula-benchmarks-20270601.csv). If this approach looks acceptable we can turn it into a single-page carveout in the SOW and walk procurement through the acceptance criteria.

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm acceptance of the operational variance language by EOD Thursday.
2) Redwood and Nebula agree a telemetry schema (we can share a template).
3) Legal/Procurement review (I’ll loop Lauran) and DocuSign for the limited exception.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call to align.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-delivery-profiles-proposal-v1.pdf (PDF, 3 pages); nebula-benchmarks-20270601.csv (CSV, 1 file)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-10T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Delivery profiles & initial rate exception — Nebula POC

Sara / team — quick technical clarifications to make the exception operationally measurable. Summarizing what we can enforce and how we'll measure it: 

1) TTFT (time-to-first-token)
   - Measurement: p95 latency from request arrival at the ingress node to first byte sent from the inference runtime.
   - Measurement window: rolling 1-minute buckets, aggregated per-region.
   - Proposed acceptable variance during POC: p95 <= 350ms for 95% of 1-minute windows; allow up to 10% of windows in the pilot to exceed up to 600ms as an "operational variance" during warm-up periods.

2) Sustained token throughput (tokens/sec per connection)
   - Measurement: sustained output rate measured over 10s sliding window per connection.
   - Target: 300 tokens/sec p95 sustained.
   - Backpressure policy: if the system detects that the per-connection rate cannot meet target for >15s, we will either (a) switch that connection to the sync endpoint for the remainder of the request or (b) elastic-burst to dedicated pool (if capacity reserved). We'll use option (a) for the POC unless Nebula requests reserved burst capacity.

3) Observable signals we'll export: request id, start_ts, first_token_ts, first_token_latency_ms, tokens_emitted, tokens_per_second (sliding windows), model_variant, region, fallback_flag. We'll provide a schema and a sample CSV (attached to Jonas' original).

If these definitions look OK to you, we can lock them into the exception language and provide instrumentation for Nebula to validate during the pilot. Happy to join a short engineering call to align on telemetry schema.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Head of Inference Product

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Sara Ortiz <sara.ortiz@nebula.ai>
Date: 2027-06-11T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Delivery profiles & initial rate exception — Nebula POC

Team — legal/ops notes on the proposed carveout: 

1) Language: prefer the term "operational variance" vs "carveout" and limit scope to the POC (explicit start/end dates).
2) SLA credits: if we include any financial credits for not meeting TTFT or sustained rate, suggest caps (e.g., credits limited to 5% of monthly invoice for the POC period) and a non-cumulative remedy.
3) Acceptance criteria: require Nebula to provide a representative traffic trace during the first 48 hours so we can calibrate thresholds. If Nebula cannot provide, the exception can be revoked with 7 days' notice.
4) Liability: no changes to indemnity/limitations; keep standard terms.

I'll draft a one-page addendum that uses the measurement language Karthik proposed, the operational variance window, and the credit caps. Jonas — I can circulate the draft for signature once we have acceptance from Nebula.

—Lauren Bishop
Lauren Bishop | Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Sara Ortiz <sara.ortiz@nebula.ai>

Subject: Re: Delivery profiles & initial rate exception — Nebula POC

Hi Jonas / Karthik —

Thanks for the clear proposal and the benchmarks. Procurement and engineering reviewed the attachment. High level feedback:

- Nebula is okay with labeling this an "operational variance" for the 30-day pilot, as long as there is a clear acceptance path and telemetry we can independently validate.
- Procurement requests a one-page summary that calls out: measurement definitions, pilot dates, credit cap, and fallback behavior (sync fallback must be explicitly visible in the API response).
- For this POC, Nebula will accept the fallback-to-sync approach rather than reserving burst capacity; we reserve the right to revisit burst options for production.

If you can send the one-pager and the draft addendum, procurement will aim to sign within 72 hours. We'll also upload our initial traffic trace to the S3 link you provide.

Best,
Sara Ortiz
Head of Integrations, Nebula AI

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>

Perfect — appreciate the quick turn. Action items and links below: 

1) Lauren to share one-page addendum (will be in my inbox by EOD tomorrow).
2) Karthik to publish telemetry schema and sample CSV — I'll share the S3 upload link with Nebula.
3) Jonas to produce a one-page summary for procurement (attached to this thread).
4) DocuSign: once the addendum is approved, we'll send the DocuSign link (preview: https://www.docusign.com/nebula/redwood-sla-exception).

Closing note: because Nebula has both bursty initial tokens and sustained throughput needs, the fallback-to-sync behavior is a safe operational compromise for the POC and lets Nebula validate UX without a full dedicated commit. For production we can revisit reserved burst or dedicated pool options.

Thanks all — I'll follow up with the one-pager and the S3 link.

—Jonas
